nodes.summary: Let $l > 1$ and $m \ge 1$ be natural numbers. Then $l^m$ can be built from exactly $m$ copies of $l$ using addition and multiplication, and every natural number that can be built from $m$ copies of $l$ in this way is at most $l^m$.
nodes.title: The largest number built from $m$ copies of $l$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l$, $k$ and $n$, the number $n$ can be built from $k$ copies of $l$ when $n$ is the value of an expression that uses exactly $k$ copies of $l$, combined by addition and multiplication with arbitrary parentheses. Inductively, $l$ is built from $1$ copy, and if $x$ is built from $a$ copies and $y$ from $b$ copies, then $x + y$ and $x y$ are built from $a + b$ copies.
nodes.title: Numbers built from copies of $l$

nodes.summary: For all positive integers $a$ and $b$, the integer complexity of $a + b$ is at most the sum of the integer complexities of $a$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Integer complexity of a sum

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert m \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a positive integer $m$, the least number of ones needed to write $m$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses. For every integer $n \ge 2$, $\lVert n \rVert$ is the least element of the set consisting of the numbers $\lVert d \rVert + \lVert n/d \rVert$ for the divisors $d \ge 2$ of $n$ and the numbers $\lVert j \rVert + \lVert n - j \rVert$ for the integers $j$…
nodes.title: Integer complexity as a minimum over factorizations and sums

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_l$ for the $l$-complexity of $n$. Let $l > 1$, let $b \ge 1$ be a multiple of $l^2$, let $a$ be a natural number with $a \le l - 1$, and let $n = b + a l$. Then $\|n\|_l = \|b\|_l + a$.
nodes.title: Adding a small multiple of $l$ to a multiple of $l^2$

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the 2-complexity of $n$. Let $m \ge 1$ and let $n$ be an even natural number with $2^m < n \le 2^{m+1}$. Then $\|n\|_2 = m + 1$ if and only if $n = 2^m + 2^t$ for some natural number $t$ with $1 \le t \le m$.
nodes.title: Even $n$ with $2^m < n \le 2^{m+1}$ and 2-complexity $m + 1$

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the 2-complexity of $n$. Let $m \ge 3$ and let $n$ be an even natural number with $2^m < n \le 2^{m+1}$. Then $\|n\|_2 = m + 2$ if and only if $n$ has one of the following forms, where all exponents are natural numbers: (a) $n = 2^m + 2^{m_2} + 2^{m_3}$ with $m > m_2 > m_3 \ge 1$; (b) $n = 2^m + 2^{m_2} + 2^{m_3} + 2^{m_4}$ with $m > m_2 > m_3 > m_4 \ge 2$ and $m + m_4 = m_2 + m_3$; (c)…
nodes.title: Even numbers in $(2^m, 2^{m+1})$ with 2-complexity $m + 2$

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the 2-complexity of $n$. Let $m \ge 3$ and let $n$ be an even natural number with $2^m < n \le 2^{m+1}$. Suppose that $n$ has one of the following forms, where all exponents are natural numbers: (a) $n = 2^m + 2^{m_2} + 2^{m_3}$ with $m > m_2 > m_3 \ge 1$; (b) $n = 2^m + 2^{m_2} + 2^{m_3} + 2^{m_4}$ with $m > m_2 > m_3 > m_4 \ge 2$ and $m + m_4 = m_2 + m_3$; (c)…
nodes.title: Four forms of even numbers with 2-complexity $m + 2$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l$ and $n$, the $l$-complexity of $n$ is $0$ if and only if there is no $k$ such that $n$ can be built from $k$ copies of $l$ using addition and multiplication.
nodes.title: The $l$-complexity vanishes exactly on numbers that cannot be built

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l$, $k$ and $n$, if $n$ can be built from $k$ copies of $l$ using addition and multiplication, then the $l$-complexity of $n$ is at most $k$.
nodes.title: The $l$-complexity is at most the size of any build

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_l$ for the $l$-complexity of $n$. For natural numbers $l > 1$ and $m \ge m' \ge 1$, $\|l^m + l^{m'}\|_l = m + 1$.
nodes.title: The $l$-complexity of $l^m + l^{m'}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l$ and $n$, if $n$ can be built from some number of copies of $l$ using addition and multiplication, then $n$ can be built in this way from $c$ copies of $l$, where $c$ is the $l$-complexity of $n$.
nodes.title: A buildable number is built from as many copies as its $l$-complexity

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the $2$-complexity of $n$. Let $S$ be a nonempty finite set of positive integers with $k$ elements and largest element $m_1$. Then $\|\sum_{e \in S} 2^e\|_2 \le m_1 + k - 1$.
nodes.title: An upper bound for the 2-complexity of a sum of distinct powers of two

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the $2$-complexity of $n$. For all natural numbers $m_1$ and $m_2$ with $m_1 > m_2 \ge 1$, one has $\|2^{m_1}\|_2 = m_1$ and $\|2^{m_1} + 2^{m_2}\|_2 = m_1 + 1$.
nodes.title: The 2-complexity of a power of two and of a sum of two powers of two

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the $2$-complexity of $n$. For all natural numbers $m$ and $r$ with $8 \le r \le 9$, one has $m + 3r - 1 \le \|2^m \cdot 6^r\|_2 \le m + 3r$.
nodes.title: Bounds for the 2-complexity of $2^m \cdot 6^r$ when $8 \le r \le 9$

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the $2$-complexity of $n$. For all natural numbers $m$ and $r$ with $1 \le r \le 7$, one has $\|2^m \cdot 6^r\|_2 = m + 3r$.
nodes.title: The 2-complexity of $2^m \cdot 6^r$ for $1 \le r \le 7$

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the $2$-complexity of $n$. For all natural numbers $m$ and $r$ with $1 \le r \le 4$, one has $\|2^m \cdot 10^r\|_2 = m + 4r$.
nodes.title: The 2-complexity of $2^m \cdot 10^r$ for $1 \le r \le 4$

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the $2$-complexity of $n$. For every natural number $m$, one has $m + 19 \le \|2^m \cdot 10^5\|_2 \le m + 20$.
nodes.title: Bounds for the 2-complexity of $2^m \cdot 10^5$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l$ and $n$, the $l$-complexity $\|n\|_l$ of $n$ is the least number $k$ such that $n$ can be built from $k$ copies of $l$ using addition and multiplication (with arbitrary parentheses), and $\|n\|_l = 0$ if $n$ cannot be built from copies of $l$ at all.
nodes.title: The $l$-complexity of a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer. If an expression $e$ has value $n$, then the integer complexity of $n$ is at most the number of ones of $e$.
nodes.title: Expressions bound the integer complexity from above

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a positive integer $n$, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses. For a positive integer $n$, let $a$ be the largest natural number with $3^a \le n$, and let $g(n) = 3a$ if $n < \frac{4}{3} \cdot 3^a$, $g(n) = 3a + 1$ if $\frac{4}{3} \cdot 3^a \le n < 2 \cdot 3^a$, and $g(n) = 3a + 2$ if $n \ge 2 \cdot 3^a$. Then…
nodes.title: The function $g$ bounds integer complexity from below

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $a$ be the largest natural number with $3^a \le n$ when $n \ge 1$, and let $a = 0$ when $n = 0$. The function $g$ on the natural numbers is given by $g(n) = 3a$ if $n < \frac{4}{3} \cdot 3^a$, $g(n) = 3a + 1$ if $\frac{4}{3} \cdot 3^a \le n < 2 \cdot 3^a$, and $g(n) = 3a + 2$ if $n \ge 2 \cdot 3^a$.
nodes.title: Lower-bound function for integer complexity

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert m \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a positive integer $m$, the least number of ones needed to write $m$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses. Let $a \le 2$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $2a + 3b \ge 2$. Then every natural number $m > 2^a 3^b$ satisfies $\lVert m \rVert > 2a + 3b$.
nodes.title: Integers above $2^a 3^b$ have complexity above $2a + 3b$ when $a \le 2$ and $2a + 3b \ge 2$

nodes.summary: For all positive integers $a$ and $b$, the integer complexity of $ab$ is at most the sum of the integer complexities of $a$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Integer complexity of a product

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a positive integer $n$, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses. For all natural numbers $a \le 2$ and $b$, not both zero, $\lVert 2^a 3^b \rVert = 2a + 3b$.
nodes.title: Integer complexity of $2^a 3^b$ for $a \le 2$

nodes.summary: The integer complexity of a positive integer $n$ is the least number of ones in an expression whose value is $n$, that is, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses.
nodes.title: Integer complexity

nodes.summary: The number of leaf selections of an $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expression, counting repetitions: a leaf counts $1$, and the count of a sum or of a product of two expressions is the sum of their counts.
nodes.title: Number of leaves of an $m$-ary expression

nodes.summary: The number of ones of an expression is the number of occurrences of the constant $1$ in it: the constant $1$ has one, and both $e_1 + e_2$ and $e_1 \times e_2$ have as many as $e_1$ and $e_2$ together.
nodes.title: Number of ones in an expression

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the value $\lVert n \rVert$ is the integer complexity of $n$ when $n$ is positive, that is, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses, and $\lVert 0 \rVert = 0$.
nodes.title: Integer complexity extended to all natural numbers

nodes.summary: The natural number expressed by an $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expression: the leaf with index $i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ has value $i + 1$, and the value of a sum or of a product of two expressions is the sum or the product of their values.
nodes.title: Value of an $m$-ary expression

nodes.summary: The value of an expression is the natural number obtained by evaluating it: the constant $1$ has value $1$, the value of $e_1 + e_2$ is the sum of the values of $e_1$ and $e_2$, and the value of $e_1 \times e_2$ is the product of their values.
nodes.title: Value of an expression

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$ there is an expression whose value is $n$.
nodes.title: Every positive integer is the value of an expression

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$, there is an $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expression whose value is $n$ (for instance a sum of ones).
nodes.title: Every positive integer has an $m$-ary expression

nodes.summary: An expression is either the constant $1$, or a sum $e_1 + e_2$ of two expressions, or a product $e_1 \times e_2$ of two expressions. Expressions are formal syntax trees, so the tree structure plays the role of parentheses.
nodes.title: Expressions built from one, addition and multiplication

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a positive integer $n$, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses. Let $P$ be a real-valued function on the natural numbers with $P(1) = 1$ such that $P(n + m) \le P(n) + P(m)$ and $P(nm) \le P(n) + P(m)$ for all positive integers $n$ and $m$. Then $P(n) \le \lVert n \rVert$ for every positive integer $n$.
nodes.title: A criterion for lower bounds on integer complexity

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_l$ for the $l$-complexity of $n$. Let $l > 1$ be a natural number and let $n$ be a positive multiple of $l$. Then $\log_l n \le \|n\|_l \le l \log_l n - 1$, where $\log_l$ is the real logarithm to base $l$.
nodes.title: Logarithmic bounds for the $l$-complexity

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the $2$-complexity of $n$. Let $n$ be a positive even integer that cannot be written as $2^a + 2^b$ with natural numbers $a \le b$. Then $\log_2 n + 1 \le \|n\|_2$.
nodes.title: A lower bound for the 2-complexity outside sums of two powers of two

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a positive integer $n$, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses. For every positive integer $n$, $\log_2(1 + n) \le \lVert n \rVert$.
nodes.title: Logarithmic lower bound for integer complexity

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the 2-complexity of $n$. Let $n \ge 1$ be an even natural number and let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers with at least five elements such that $n = \sum_{e \in S} 2^e$. Then $\log_2 n + 2 \le \|n\|_2$, where $\log_2$ is the real base-2 logarithm.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the 2-complexity of even sums of five or more distinct powers of two

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the 2-complexity of $n$: the least number of copies of $2$ from which $n$ can be built using addition and multiplication, and $0$ if $n$ cannot be built. Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n$ even, $n \ge 1$ and $2^m < n \le 2^{m+1}$. Suppose that $n \ne 2^a + 2^b$ for all natural numbers $a \le b$, and that $n$ has none of Zhang's four exceptional forms for $m$. Then…
nodes.title: Lower bound $\log_2 n + 2$ for the 2-complexity (Zhang's Corollary 4)

nodes.summary: Write $\|n\|_2$ for the 2-complexity of $n$: the least number of copies of $2$ from which $n$ can be built using addition and multiplication, and $0$ if $n$ cannot be built. For every even natural number $n \ge 1$, $\log_2 n \le \|n\|_2 \le 2 \log_2 n - 1$, where $\log_2$ is the real base-2 logarithm.
nodes.title: Logarithmic bounds for the 2-complexity (Zhang's Lemma 3(3))

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the $2$-ary (binary) Mahler–Popken complexity $\|n\|_2$ satisfies $\log_2 n \le \|n\|_2$.
nodes.title: Logarithmic lower bound for the binary Mahler–Popken complexity

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m \ge 1$, $a \ge 1$ and $b \ge 1$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\|\cdot\|_m$ satisfies $\|a + b\|_m \le \|a\|_m + \|b\|_m$.
nodes.title: Subadditivity of the $m$-ary complexity under addition

nodes.summary: For every natural number $m \ge 1$ there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\|n\|_m$ equals the right-hand side of the recursion (9), that is, the least of the values $\|d\|_m + \|n/d\|_m$ over divisors $d$ of $n$ with $d \ne 1$ and $d \ne n$, and the values $\|\eta\|_m + \|n - \eta\|_m$ over $0 < \eta < n$.
nodes.title: The $m$-ary complexity eventually satisfies its recursion

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$ and every $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expression $e$ whose value is $n$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\|n\|_m$ is at most the number of leaves of $e$.
nodes.title: Expressions bound the $m$-ary complexity from above

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m \ge 1$, $a \ge 1$ and $b \ge 1$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\|\cdot\|_m$ satisfies $\|a b\|_m \le \|a\|_m + \|b\|_m$.
nodes.title: Subadditivity of the $m$-ary complexity under multiplication

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the $1$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\|n\|_1$ equals the classical integer complexity of $n$, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses.
nodes.title: The $1$-ary complexity is the integer complexity

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\|n\|_m$ is positive.
nodes.title: The $m$-ary complexity is positive

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$, there is an $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expression whose value is $n$ and whose number of leaves (counted with repetition) equals the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\lVert n \rVert_m$.
nodes.title: The Mahler–Popken complexity is attained

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 3$, the binary ($2$-ary) Mahler–Popken complexity $\lVert n \rVert_2$ equals the minimum of the sums $\lVert d \rVert_2 + \lVert n/d \rVert_2$ over the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $d \ne 1$ and $d \ne n$, and of the sums $\lVert \eta \rVert_2 + \lVert n - \eta \rVert_2$ over $0 < \eta < n$. This is the recursion (9) for $m = 2$.
nodes.title: Recursion for the binary Mahler–Popken complexity

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the binary ($2$-ary) Mahler–Popken complexity $\lVert n \rVert_2$ is at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + \nu_2(n) - 1$, where $\nu_2(n)$ is the number of ones in the base-$2$ expansion of $n$.
nodes.title: Upper bound for the binary Mahler–Popken complexity

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity $\lVert n \rVert_m$ is the smallest number of leaves (counted with repetition) of an $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expression whose value is $n$: the smallest number of possibly repeated selections from $\{1, \dots, m\}$ needed to express $n$ with addition, multiplication and legal bracketing. If no expression has value $n$ (which happens exactly when…
nodes.title: Mahler–Popken complexity

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expressions are the formal expressions built from leaves using the binary operations $+$ and $\times$; the tree structure plays the role of brackets. Each leaf carries a label $i \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ (so there are $m$ kinds of leaf), and a leaf with label $i$ stands for the number $i + 1 \in \{1, \dots, m\}$.
nodes.title: Mahler–Popken expressions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, write $\lVert k \rVert_m$ for the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken complexity of $k$. The recursion value of $n$ is the smallest of the sums $\lVert d \rVert_m + \lVert n/d \rVert_m$ over the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $d \ne 1$ and $d \ne n$, and of the sums $\lVert \eta \rVert_m + \lVert n - \eta \rVert_m$ over $0 < \eta < n$; it is $0$ when there are no such sums. This is the right-hand side…
nodes.title: Right-hand side of the Mahler–Popken recursion

nodes.summary: The translation of an expression built from one, addition and multiplication into a $1$-ary Mahler–Popken expression replaces each occurrence of $1$ by the leaf standing for $1$ and keeps every addition and multiplication, so the expression tree is unchanged.
nodes.title: Integer-complexity expressions as $1$-ary Mahler–Popken expressions

nodes.summary: If $n$ can be obtained from $k$ copies of $l$ using addition and multiplication, then $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Every build uses at least one copy

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$ and a natural number $c$, the predicate holds when some expression has value $n$ and exactly $c$ ones.
nodes.title: Achievable numbers of ones

nodes.summary: The translation of a $1$-ary Mahler–Popken expression into an expression built from one, addition and multiplication replaces each leaf (the only leaf stands for $1$) by $1$ and keeps every addition and multiplication, so the expression tree is unchanged.
nodes.title: $1$-ary Mahler–Popken expressions as integer-complexity expressions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, $n$ has one of the four exceptional forms for $m$ when one of the following holds: (a) $n = 2^m + 2^{m_2} + 2^{m_3}$ for some natural numbers $m > m_2 > m_3 \ge 1$; (b) $n = 2^m + 2^{m_2} + 2^{m_3} + 2^{m_4}$ for some natural numbers $m > m_2 > m_3 > m_4 \ge 2$ with $m + m_4 = m_2 + m_3$; (c) $n = 2^m + 2^{m-3} + 2^{m_2} + 2^{m_2 - 1}$ for some natural number $m_2$ with…
nodes.title: Zhang's four exceptional forms
Number Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
